exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: A compact brand guide with typography, color roles, writing examples, and usage checks.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This Claw Me example uses the shared Archivo and Bitter fonts, quiet surfaces, green actions, and coral brand accents. The guide is a practical companion to the bundled Tailwind source.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Role: Body and controls · Token or family: Archivo · Use: Readable text, labels, and data
Role: Document headings · Token or family: Bitter · Use: Clear content hierarchy
Role: Primary action · Token or family: Green ink on light surface · Use: Links and active choices
Role: Accent · Token or family: Coral · Use: Small brand marker
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Typography in use: Use Archivo for operational labels and dense information. Use Bitter for document headings. Keep headings descriptive and avoid squeezing text with excessive letter spacing.
Color with a purpose: The green accent identifies a useful next action or active state. Status labels need words as well as color. White and quiet neutral surfaces keep long documents readable.
Write like a colleague: Prefer “Review the project brief” to “Unlock your project potential.” State what a control does and describe an outcome that the artifact can actually support. Keep implementation notes in source documentation.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: specimen layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
